profile.bio: I write Go services and run the machines under them, mostly where a number has to survive an audit. Ten years across energy and software: four managing the asset data behind a solar portfolio above $100M, a founder's desk building risk and trading models for energy companies, and now platform and security work on a fleet I rebuild from one repository.

projects.title: Clean Energy Asset & Telemetry Platform
projects.description: For four years I ran the numbers behind a solar portfolio above $100M: valuation and yield models that had to satisfy bank auditors, mobile capture for field technicians, and counterparty hedging when a deal needed one. The part I am proudest of is the reconciliation: when a sensor died, the model said so instead of quietly reporting a good month.
projects.impact: Bank-audited models across $100M+ of assets, and due diligence work alongside institutional lenders and tax equity.

projects.title: fibtransponder: Fibonacci Streaming State Machine
projects.description: I wanted a stream detector with a bounded cost per step, so I wrote the benchmark before believing the design. It failed on natural text, and the claim narrowed to the structure itself — which is the result I would rather show.
projects.impact: Showed that adjacency width works as a locality selector, and falsified the seed-only detector with a corpus benchmark.

projects.title: Multi-Host Declarative NixOS Infrastructure
projects.description: Thirteen machines — a NAS, workstations, an internet-facing host, a remote builder — rebuilt from one repository. Secrets are encrypted per host, certificates rotate on a schedule, and commissioning a new host is a commit plus one command.
projects.impact: No host carries its own install notes. A host can be rebuilt, audited or handed over from the repository alone.

projects.title: Bountystash: Deterministic Work Engine
projects.description: A request arrives as prose and has drifted by the time the work is done. Bountystash records it as an immutable document: state is a replay of events, one binary serves HTML, JSON and a terminal UI, and every endpoint answers curl.
projects.impact: A single binary with no frontend build, and an audit trail that reconstructs what was agreed a month later.

philosophy.title: If I cannot rebuild it, it is not running
philosophy.body: A server, a document or a binary that exists only in its current state is a thing I have to guess about later. Nix flakes and locked dependencies remove a class of failure I would rather not debug at three in the morning.

philosophy.title: Learn the domain before the schema
philosophy.body: Yield formulas, physical constraints, and how a lender reads a report all change the design before the first table exists. Writing the code is the easy part.

philosophy.title: Keep the runtime small enough to reason about
philosophy.body: Compiled Go, clean data models, server-rendered HTML, and respect for a 14 KB budget. Latency comes from fundamentals, not from a framework.
